newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Panel tells Arafat officials must face trial.
newsitem.headline: Panel tells Arafat officials must face trial.

text.p: A committee appointed by Palestinian President Yasser Arafat to investigate corruption concluded on Monday he must swiftly enact stringent reforms and that some officials must be put on trial.

"We have discovered serious shortcomings and there are people who are involved who should be put on trial," said Tayeb Abdel-Rahim, head of the presidential committee on corruption which submitted a 127-page report to Arafat.

Abdel-Rahim told Reuters that Arafat had promised to take "immediate, firm action" in line with the recommendations. Arafat in June ordered an inquiry into an auditor's report that members of his administration squandered $326 million in public funds last year.

"There is no squandering of money, but I think there is more than that. There is an administrative imbalance and an absence of regulations and other violations resulting from lack of experience," Abdel-Rahim said.

He would not say which officials were recommended for questioning, removal or trial. Majid al-Muzainy, a committee member and judge of the high justice court, said some senior officials were among those criticised.

"(There were) ministers and deputies and others, and we suggested some measures that will satisfy all the people," he told reporters. An opinion poll in June showed most Palestinians would support an initiatave by Palestinian legislators to bring down Arafat's government over corruption.
